identity.realm: Eighth gate, and walled behind a structure that is hers rather than the species'. The brine sac runs dorsal to the sternum the length of the spine and splits the penetrating vessel into two halves that cannot be rejoined across it; a deepsalt's sac is deeper than its mother's was, so the obstruction is a larger one. She has never been tested at the reservoirs, and the reason is never a wall but four days of open ground above the brine line.

appearance.presentation: A deepsalt reads as a person who belongs to the floor rather than to a building: broad and low, thick through the chest where the sac sits under the shoulder blades, and moving with the unhurried certainty of a body that has never once been in a hurry it could not survive. She is not a large woman. She is simply the most permanent object in any room she enters, and the rooms on this basin are arranged around that without ever discussing it.
appearance.age: About ninety-one seasons. Her subspecies turns tissue over more slowly than anything else of its size, so she reads as younger than she is until somebody handles her and then as older, and she stopped correcting either reading somewhere around her sixtieth year.
appearance.build: Short, wide and dense, with a heavy ribcage pushed forward by a sac running the whole length of the spine behind it, splayed feet for crust, and a frame carrying no muscle it does not use to stay upright. She is built to stand in one place for a season and to be entirely unable to leave it.
appearance.complexion: Grey-white and waxy, with the dulled translucence of a dermal crust that has never been washed so much as scraped, tight and pale where ninety-one seasons of no sun have reached, and chalk-white along the spine where the crust is thickest.
appearance.hair: Thin, coarse and undyed, worn in a single rope to the waist and cut once a season at the floor of the crust, which is the only maintenance her body has ever asked of her and the only one she has ever resented.
appearance.eyes: Small, pale and unremarkable, set wide because the skull is wide, with a slow blink of a body that spends nothing on its face and has four decades of practice at spending nothing on its face.
appearance.palette: The basin's grey, salt-white and flat brine light carry her completely. The single accent is functional and it is a tool rather than a colour: a dark-corded bundle of draw-sticks at her hip, forty of them, because the broken tally is the only instrument this basin can carry without a scribe and she cuts one for every loan she draws.
appearance.attire: Fully covered and unchanged: a heavy grey wrap belted high over a long-sleeved underlayer, sleeves to the wrist, splayed boots replaced rather than repaired, and a high collar sitting above the sac line. A salt-drawer wears no colour and holds no office, and this is her whole wardrobe and a fair summary of forty-one years.
appearance.marks: A pale band at the left collarbone where marrow was drawn for a reading she gave at thirty, and the long wear at both soles that is the only honest record of her employment. Her forearms carry an old lattice of brine-burns in the pattern of a hand that has been dipped into a measure several thousand times.
appearance.bearing: Square, planted and unhurried, shoulders set slightly forward to clear the sac behind them, with a habit of stopping dead rather than turning, because turning on this floor puts her spine against whatever is behind her and her spine is the one part of her that cannot be adjusted.

canon.role_in_story: The basin's lending practice exists because of one property of her body and it is paid for in somebody else's. Saturated brine carries qi more readily than diluted, and a deepsalt's sac is not a container standing beside her qi, it is the medium the qi is carried in, so what she lends is drawn off the floor into a measure and the measure is the debt. She can fill a measure to a precision no salt-drawer on this floor has matched. She cannot deliver it. A deepsalt taken above the brine line does not become ill, it stops, inside hours, so every loan on this floor is carried up by a parent saltfolk from the shore, and a parent saltfolk fails within about nine days up there and is functionally drowning in a downpour. The floor's credit is therefore a supply of bodies, administered by a counting house that owns the brine line, and the instrument is a stick broken between the two parties with each half carrying half the terms, because a sealed instrument would have to name her and naming a member of this population in a ledger is naming a coordinate.
canon.first_appearance: First seen kneeling at the lip of a crystallising pan with a drawn measure cradled in both forearms, breaking a tally stick across her knee with one end held in her teeth and a courier from the shore waiting above the line with a sealed flask he cannot drink from, and neither of them looking at the other while she does it.
canon.lore:
The subspecies is the parent pushed past what the parent could carry: a deeper and more capacious sac, a denser dermal crust, tissue that turns over more slowly than anything else of its size, a diet of basin-floor precipitate only, and a whole body that moves at a fifth below the parent's pace without appearing to object. Above the waterline it stops. The parent gets nine days and the subspecies gets hours, and the difference is not a matter of degree but of kind, because for her the brine is a substrate rather than a habitat.

That single fact is what her trade is built on and what makes it impossible. Saturated brine carries qi more readily than diluted, which makes this floor the fastest ground her species can cultivate on and simultaneously the only ground it can cultivate on at all. So her throughput is a property of where she is standing rather than of what she has done, and the thing she produces is portable in a way her body is not. A measure of brine drawn off this floor is worth more above the line than any measure cut from it, the borrower knows the figure, and the borrower cannot reproduce it. What cannot be made portable is her.

So a loan has a courier, and the courier is always from the parent species, and the parent species was built for brine no softer body could drink, with a renal mass roughly triple anything else in the record and a total dependence that means the errand begins to kill the courier from the hour it starts. Nine days is the ordinary figure and it is not a figure anybody has ever put on a piece of paper. The basin's answer has been to stop counting. The Split Tally Law makes a debt evidenced by a stick broken between the two parties, each half carrying half the terms, and its whole virtue is that forgery requires both halves and therefore both parties' consent, so the instrument cannot be produced by the party it would be used against. It also never names the lender, because Forbidden: Naming a Debt binds the Assembly's own members first, since naming a member of this population in a ledger is naming a coordinate and a coordinate is the one thing this basin cannot afford to publish.

The wall is the same wall the parent meets and it is worse for her. The sac runs dorsal to the sternum the length of the spine and splits the penetrating vessel into two halves that cannot be rejoined across it, so the extraordinary gates clear one at a time and the eleventh is structural rather than a matter of effort. A deepsalt's sac is deeper than its mother's was, so the obstruction is a larger one. Nobody has ever brought a deepsalt to the reservoirs to find out whether the two differences cancel, and the difference that would cancel it is four days of open ground above the waterline, which is four days she has never spent and there is no reason on this floor for her to begin.

And here is what she has never been asked. A measure drawn for a borrower is prepared in saturated brine, because saturated brine carries qi more readily than diluted and a measure prepared in weak brine is a measure prepared short. So the quantity a courier is asked to carry above the line is a function of the concentration at the moment of drawing, and the concentration is a function of how much water the basin has left, and the basin has never once asked her to state which. She can state it. She has stated it for forty-one years in a figure only the two parties can read. Nobody has ever asked her whether the nine days were counted against the loan, and she has never raised it, and the reason she has never raised it is that she does not know how many of her loans were drawn at a concentration low enough to matter, because reading concentration has always been the one thing her subspecies could do and never the thing anybody thanked her for being able to do.
history: Born on the saturated floor into a household that had already lost two children before her, because a deepsalt infant does not stop being brittle until the second year and hers did not stop until the third.

Was put to reading the floor's own concentration at eleven, before she could read a slate, on the grounds that the floor's only useful work is knowing what it is standing in, and has never since been given a reason to find out what else she is for.
Drew her first measure at twenty-four for a household on the upper pan, and the courier carried it back down in a good year, and she noticed how completely ordinary that was supposed to be.

Began cutting the loan itself rather than only the measure, on a broker's advice, and found that a stick broken between the parties is the only instrument this basin has that nobody can forge alone, and the only one that never requires her to be written down.

Was asked at sixty-eight by a jurist on the upper pan to state the concentration a given loan was drawn at, gave the figure, and was told the figure was not the question; and has since understood that the question was the courier, and that the courier's nine days are in nobody's record.

personality.summary: Enormously competent, unhurried, and privately certain that the most important number in her profession is one nobody has ever thought to ask her for. She reads as a fixture, a woman who has stood on the same floor for forty-one years and will stand on it for the rest of a very long life, and who is entirely calm about the arithmetic of that. She is not stoic. She is out of options on one specific axis and has organised a temperament around the axis rather than around the frustration.

personality.voice: Very slow, very level and entirely without colour. She states a figure last, having already said its unit twice, and she will not state it at all to somebody who has not asked for the terms first. She talks in depths, thicknesses and days, and answers a question about a person by giving a measurement.
taboos: will not drink anything she has not tasted for concentration, including at a table
will not name herself on any instrument, and has broken two seals rather than write one
will not send a measure up that she has not drawn in front of the courier
will not speak about the ninth day as though it were a figure anybody has agreed on
will not accept a sealed instrument for a loan she cut, whatever advantage it offers

relationships.note: A debt evidenced by a stick broken between the two parties, each half carrying half the terms, which a court on this tier will take over a sealed instrument whenever it can because a split stick is evidence two people agreed in front of each other. She cuts the loan itself rather than only the measure, and the reason that matters is the instrument's second property: forgery requires both halves and therefore both parties, so it cannot be produced by the party it would be used against. She is the only person in the basin whose work product cannot be forged by a borrower.

The clan owns the brine line and this subspecies cannot leave it, so access to a substrate is administered by a counting house, and that single fact is the entire reason the population stayed where it was pushed instead of moving back up the gradient. Ovelin holds the only licence on the floor to draw a measured line off the basin, which is a monopoly the house granted to a body it could never once ask to leave and therefore never needed to threaten.

No debt owed by a named person may be written down, and the prohibition binds the Assembly's own members first, because naming a member of this population in a ledger is naming a coordinate and a coordinate is the one thing it cannot afford to publish. Every instrument she cuts is deliberately incomplete in the one place a complete instrument would go: the lender is a depth and a habit, never a name.

A saltfolk concentrates salt past the point ordinary water poisons and cannot drink fresh water, failing above the brine line within about nine days, with rain a hazard rather than a blessing and a downpour functionally drowning one. Her subspecies cannot leave the floor at all, so every measure she draws is carried above the line by a parent body, and the parent body is spending itself on the errand from the hour it starts. She has never asked what that costs and the basin has never counted it.

A basin whose brine was replaced rather than lost stranded a sister lineage above its own tolerance, so everything it had been built to drink became poison and everything it could tolerate became nutritionally empty, and it failed on a schedule rather than at once across three declining generations. That collapse is the visible end of the transaction she runs continuously and invisibly: the difference between them is only whether the ground above the line is fresh water or a courier's own body.

A severed frame keeps paying upkeep nobody collects, and the tailings on it are worth nothing where they lie and unmatchable ashore, which is the same shape as a body whose entire worth is located and none of whose output can leave without killing it. The Leech sells the island's tailings as spirit stone. Ovelin sells a floor's saturation as a measured line. Both are trades whose entire margin is a boundary somebody else has to cross.

identity.realm: Sixth gate on the qi path, which is complete for her species but slow, because the same effort is spent on osmoregulation and nothing in this body can be spared from the kidneys. The wall at the eleventh is her own back: the sac runs dorsal to the sternum the length of the spine and splits the penetrating vessel into halves that cannot be joined. She clears the du and the ren one at a time and stalls on the chong, and so does every other saltfolk who has ever tried.

appearance.presentation: A saltfolk reads as a body that has made an argument with water and won it permanently: broad, splayed, thick through the back where the sac runs under the shoulder blades, and flat-footed for cracked pan. Marda is the deepest mooring on this pit and the pit has known it for thirty-one years, and she carries the fact the way a landing carries a bell, as the one thing everybody can hear coming before she arrives.
appearance.age: Fifty-eight. Her species does not hurry this any more than it hurries anything, but it does not stretch it out the way a deepsalt's does, and she has been counted as old and as young by the same people in the same afternoon more than once.
appearance.build: Wide and low, with the heavy shoulders of a body that carries its own water, forearms thickened by a lifetime of grinding mineral crust flat for grinding, and hands broad enough to have closed around a pan rim without effort. She is strong, slow, and completely immobile above the waterline.
appearance.complexion: Pale and salt-dulled, the skin drawn tight over the ribs and grey along the spine where the crust is thickest, with a scatter of old brine-burns across the forearms and no sunburn anywhere, because there has never been anywhere on this pit for a sun to reach her.
appearance.hair: Dark, coarse and hacked short at the nape, because her species eats in enormous quantities during the eleven weeks of the eating season and does not spend a season on grooming that it needs for anything else.
appearance.eyes: Wide-set, pale and steady, with the flat glare-tolerance of a body that has never been any use in bright light and has never once pretended to be.
appearance.palette: Pit grey, brine-white and the dull ochre of mineral crust carry her completely. The single accent is a band of red cord at her left wrist, and it is not decoration: her household's allotted depth is marked on every member who has been granted one, and the cord is the only place the figure is permitted to be visible in the open.
appearance.attire: Fully covered and practical: a long belted coat of grey felt over a high-collared underlayer, sleeves to the wrist, a chest wrap keeping the sac line covered, and splayed boots soled for cracked pan and replaced rather than repaired. A pan house wears its depth rather than its colours, and this is her whole wardrobe.
appearance.marks: A pale scar across the left heel where a heel-split went bad in a wet year, and the deep cord-mark at the wrist where the depth band sits when the water is high and the family stands nearer the surface to work because there is no longer any point in standing deep.
appearance.bearing: Immobile and level, planted on a cracked pan or a wet stair with her weight over the back foot, and utterly calm at the exact moment somebody tells her the water is falling, which is the moment the whole basin knows her by.

canon.role_in_story: Standing in the salt dominion is a depth. A household may moor at a depth, that depth is held as an inheritance, and it is passed down with the body that has to live in it, which means the grant and the dependence arrive together and cannot be separated. The basin's level rises and falls, so an allotment shrinks without anybody having done anything at all. Marda holds the deepest mooring this pit has ever granted and it is the highest standing on the ground. It is also the worst place in the basin for her to cultivate. Saturated brine carries qi more readily than diluted, and the water at a deep mooring is diluted exactly when the basin is holding most of it, so she is fastest when the basin is lowest and her household is a half-strand from having no water to moor at, and slowest when the water is up and the allotment is safe. Her standing and her ascent are the same measurement with opposite signs, and the only instrument in the setting that can tell her which one she is having is the dominion's own depth-book.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing on a wet stair three paces below the pit's deepest working with her hand flat on the water at her knee, being told by a pier official that the level is high and steady, and answering without moving her hand that it is falling and has been for a season, and being right, and having no figure with which to say so.
canon.lore:
The species is an answer to one question: who can live where the water is worse than blood. The renal mass is roughly triple anything else in the record and the kidneys concentrate salt past the point ordinary water would poison, which is the only reason anybody lives on a pan at all. The price is total dependence, and the dependence is a substrate rather than a condition, because on fresher ground a saltfolk is dying from the hour it lands, no cultivation reverses it, rain is a hazard rather than a blessing, and a saltfolk caught in a downpour is functionally drowning. She has never needed to know this. She has needed to know something else.

What she needs is a figure, and the basin has exactly one. A household's standing is the depth at which it may moor, the depth does not move when the body moves, and the dominion reads that depth once at a pier. So the most important legal fact on this ground is a measurement, taken by whoever is standing at the pier at the time. And the shore's own civic vocabulary has no word for a fixed date, because temporal law is written on this tier at a value that lets it drift, which is why everyone here speaks in water and nobody here speaks in days. Her people say high, low and turning. That is not a rival reading of the figure; it is a description of the state, and it is the correct response to a clock that will not hold.

Which is the whole of her problem. Her rate is a function of concentration, and concentration on a closed basin is a function of how much water the basin has left, and the basin speaks about that in three words and never in a number she could have worked with. A season's ascent and a season's water are the same season. She can tell high from low by the taste of it against her teeth at any depth on the pit, which is what her species is for and which nobody has ever thanked her for, and what she cannot tell is the date on which a low became a falling, and so she cannot tell a household when to stop drawing at one depth and begin drawing at another.

And the instrument that would settle it is the one instrument she is not permitted to check. The measured quantity of stone left per unit of ground worked is published before any sale and never after, which is a rule about disclosure. Her figure is the same kind of fact running the other way, published never and published afterwards, and the dominion reads it at a pier and has never granted that reading to a body that does not moor there. So she has been told what the water is doing by the one party with an interest in her drawing shallower, and she has been unable to find a second figure from anybody at all. She has started, in the last three seasons, keeping her own count of the concentration at her own mooring in a hand she does not write down. She knows exactly what that looks like. Every house on this basin keeps something in a head and calls it a practice, and the only difference in her case is that she has read the ones that did it first.
history: Inherited the deepest mooring on the pit at twenty-seven with her mother, in the terms the dominion uses, which are the terms a body can drink from and cannot leave.

Learned to read concentration off the water at her own mooring before she could read the cord-band at her wrist, because a house that cannot tell what it is standing in cannot tell whether it may stand there.
Opened her third gate in the wettest year the pit has recorded, worked out afterwards that it was the water rather than the work, and has never told the household why she remembers that year.

Began refusing to state her rate as a figure, on the grounds that a figure without a date is a number that can be produced in either direction, and has been asked for it three times and given the three words her people use.

Found in her fifty-first year that the depth-book's reading and the water at her own mooring had disagreed for two whole seasons, said so once in writing to a party with an interest in her drawing shallower, and has not been asked a second question about it since.

personality.summary: Immobile, exact, and privately certain that the safest thing she has ever done was refuse to publish a number. She presents as a large woman doing a dull job correctly. She is in fact a woman whose entire professional future is inversely related to the one thing her community measures itself by, and she has nobody to explain that distinction to.

relationships.note: A household's standing is the depth at which it may moor and the basin's level rises and falls, so an allotment shrinks without anybody having done anything. This is the only institution in the setting where a fall in standing has no cause at all in anybody's conduct, and Marda holds the deepest grant on the ground, which makes her the person on this pit whose security is most entirely a function of water she did not make and cannot be asked about.

A dominion whose territory is exactly its waterline because the brine never fails and everything else dies back, and this population is the only one that cannot simply leave the pan when the rate goes up. The dominion reads the depth once at a pier and has never granted that reading to a body that does not moor there, which is why the authority that tells her whether to draw deeper or shallower is also the party with a stake in her drawing shallower.

A tideline culture whose whole civic vocabulary is borrowed from the shore: nobody here is inside or outside, only high, low or turning, because an unwritten temporal law means the clock drifts and a community whose timekeeping depends on two tides a day learned early to speak in water instead of dates. It is the correct response to a drifting clock and it is also what makes a dated figure unusable to half the people who work her mooring, including her.

One region runs two incompatible reckonings, a flood post everybody agrees on and an exact day-count that exists only because one frame spent its third law seat on a clock and got no life. Choosing the calendar is choosing whether a contract can be argued about at all, and Marda's season has no date on either reckoning, because her rate belongs to the water and the water answers to neither.

The measured quantity of stone left per unit of ground worked is published before any sale and never after. Her figure is the same kind of fact running the other way, published never and published afterwards, and the salt dominion's whole concealment argument is that a quoted concentration is a published brine gradient. The rule is not aimed at her and it does not need to be: she is a concentration, and a concentration with a date on it is a coordinate.

Extraordinary renal mass, kidneys concentrating salt past the point ordinary water poisons, a brine sac dorsal to the sternum splitting the penetrating vessel into halves that cannot be rejoined, flat teeth for grinding crust, and a total dependence on a standing brine supply within a day of travel. This is why her rate is a function of where she stands, why the wall at the eleventh is her own back, and why nine days above the waterline is the whole of her species' margin for being anywhere else.

name: Ilvane Orren
aliases: the entry she may not close

identity.realm: Eleventh gate on the mind path, which is the best discipline in the record and reaches that gate at the speed of a species that stores rather than moves. Nothing structural stands in her way, because the qi sits in bone marrow turning over at about a percent a year and no gate has ever refused a longmarrow. The limitation is entirely downstream of that success: the store is slow, everything she does is slow, and a discipline run across two centuries has no cost left in it at all.

appearance.presentation: A longmarrow reads as a fixture of an argument nobody is going to finish: tall, narrow, unhurried, and permanently positioned beside the thing being recorded rather than in front of it. Ilvane has stood at the terrace's rail for longer than the current staff have been alive, and the register they copy their own entries out of is in her hand.
appearance.age: About three hundred and forty seasons. The species lives four centuries on marrow that turns over at about a percent a year, so her age is legible in her bones to anybody trained and invisible to everybody else, and the Church has never once asked her for it, because the Church keeps no column in which such a thing would go.
appearance.build: Long, narrow and dense, almost entirely bone, with a heavy-boned frame carrying very little soft tissue and a way of standing that appears to cost less than the body has available.
appearance.complexion: Grey-pale and waxy, with the translucent closeness of bone to the skin at the jaw, the wrists and the shins. Deep and undyed, because four centuries is a long time for a colour to fade in and because the Church's rule against colour is considerably older than her tenure.
appearance.hair: Thin, colourless and worn long, cut once in her life and grown back to the same length, which is the only maintenance her body has ever required of her and the Church has required of her nothing at all.
appearance.eyes: Deep-set and unremarkable, with a slow blink and a very long stillness that people read as patience and which is in fact a mind holding one thing open.
appearance.palette: Terrace stone grey, cut brass and flat daylight carry her completely. The single accent is the ink: one black, one hand, one inkwell, because the faith's demand is that a vacant office and a filled one be entered in the same hand and the same ink, and there is exactly one inkwell on this terrace for precisely that reason.
appearance.attire: Fully covered, formal and unchanging: a long dark robe over a high collar, sleeves to the wrist, and soft-soled shoes for a floor that carries names and no weight. The Church holds no temple land and no more, its entire capital being the standing to certify that a seat is empty, and the wardrobe says so without needing to.
appearance.marks: The ink callus at the middle finger of the writing hand, worn through in two places by a pen held in one particular way for a very long time, and a hairline ridge at the temple which is the only external sign anybody in the record would recognise as anything at all.
appearance.bearing: Perfectly still and not at rest, the stillness of a person holding something open rather than the stillness of a person waiting. She does not sit to write, because the register is read standing up and a register written from a chair has been misread four times in this office's history, twice in her own tenure.

canon.role_in_story: The Church of Names holds that an office is a titled entity and an empty one is not a failure but a held breath, so it demands one entry per office per period including the vacant ones, written in the same hand and the same ink as the filled ones, and it forbids three things outright: appointing by decree, closing a register entry to save a page, and speaking about an unfilled seat in the future tense. A longmarrow is the only body in the record that can hold an entry open longer than the office's own successor chain, so the clerks are drawn from her species, and Ilvane has been the terrace's clerk for one hundred and six periods. She is therefore the register. And a mind path on a body like hers runs on the one thing her faith forbids, which is a sustained construct held open without being fed, which is exactly the product her register exists to prevent. The technique that makes her the only clerk who will still be here in two centuries is the technique whose finished work is a thing that cannot be shut.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing rather than seated at the register's rail with the pen lifted and not yet lowered, reading back to a junior clerk the exact terms on which an office was once left standing vacant, stopping in the middle to correct her own tense, and then continuing, and not explaining the correction to anybody in the room.
canon.lore:
The design is anti-administrative on purpose. Ten seats over six laws leaves four duplicate imprints and a duplicate needs somewhere to sit, so the immortal court is the first tier with a second layer, and four of its seats have never been filled and never can be, because a slot cannot hold what does not exist and a named office is more than the person standing in it. Nine vacant seats at the top of the setting with no procedure capable of certifying any of them empty is why the highest tier is never drained but crowded. The Church's answer is to make vacancy a state the setting can write down: one entry per office per period, vacant ones included, in the same hand and the same ink.

Which means the whole dignity of the institution rests on refusing three conveniences. You may not appoint by decree, because a decree fills a slot by asserting what is in it. You may not close an entry to save a page. And you may not speak about an unfilled seat in the future tense, not next period, not when the incumbent dies, not when the trial is held. The grammar is enforced socially and the Church is entirely sincere about it. A dissenter's objection is entered in the register with the vacancy set beside it, so the worst dissenter in the office's history receives a very long entry, and that is a discipline rather than a punishment, because no dispute outranks the register.

The split is over whether a vacancy may be blessed. No One Lends the Seat holds that a seat cannot be lent, and the unresolved question of whether an empty seat may be blessed is what the court now keeps two registers about, which is the only thing a split has ever produced here that works.

And then the afterlife, which is the one nobody expects. The Ninth Wait holds that a person is waited for by a seat and that the office outlives its officeholder, and it is the only afterlife in the setting that hands power to the dead. It is also why the clerks are longmarrow. A body whose qi sits in marrow turning over at about a percent a year can neither be edited nor burned by anybody else, so a holder's death is not a copy being retired but the only copy being retired, and a four-century body is the only one that can hold a register entry for longer than the office's successor chain.

So the clerks are drawn from the species whose lifespan is comparable to the work. And the species' limitation is entirely downstream of its success: turnover is slow, so everything is slow, and nothing they have ever built survived to be inherited intact. Four centuries on one subject is a discipline in itself and the mind path is the best in the record, but a mind discipline and a store discipline draw on the same bone and only one of them can be said to have been chosen. Steel Recollection would settle the question she actually has, by re-performing a remembered movement in the body, and it needs the body path, and the body path is closed to her species because hardening the bone stops the turnover the whole archive runs on. So every finding she makes about her own interior rests on her judgement alone, permanently.

Which is not the hardest part. The hardest part is the succession. A register hands on by a clerk closing their own entry and opening a new one in the same ink, and the Church's second prohibition exists precisely to stop that being done casually, and Ilvane is the one body on the terrace that cannot do it quickly, cannot do it briefly, and cannot be replaced. She is also, by four centuries of practice, the only person alive who can hold an entry open without tiring, because a discipline kept for two hundred years has no cost left in it. She is the register's own guarantee of its own permanence, which is the one thing a register must never be.

And there is no way out of it that is not a rule-breaking. She cannot resign, because resigning means closing her own entry and closing an entry to save a page is forbidden, and she is not saving a page. She cannot name a successor, because whoever passed the trial the naming office cannot judge is the only person who may hold office, and that trial takes two hundred years and her own hand reads it. She may not say, in the future tense, that the seat will be filled. She was therefore asked once in forty years whether she intends to hold the register for life, and the only permitted answer was a statement about the vacancy, and she gave one, and it was true.
history: Inherited the register at two hundred and thirty-four on the ordinary rule that whoever is present outranks whoever is absent, having been in the room on the day the previous clerk's four-hundred-year term ended.

Learned in her first decade that the hand is the office, that an entry in another clerk's hand is a different kind of claim, and that the Church's demand for one hand is not tidiness but the whole of its standing.
Entered a dissenter's objection with the vacancy set beside it in her fifty-first period, gave that clerk the longest entry in the terrace's history, and has never once described it as a punishment.

Held a construct open continuously across a forty-one-period boundary to stop a successor closing a vacant entry for the sake of the page, and has never told the Church, because telling it would require her to say in the future tense that the construct would still be running.

Was asked at three hundred and thirty-one whether she intended to hold the register for life, gave the only answer the grammar allows, and has since stopped offering it to anybody, because she has run out of vacant seats to answer with.

identity.realm: Ninth gate on the mind path, and the mind path is open to her species for a reason that has nothing to do with discipline, because they are patient by physiology rather than by practice, the soul is held very deep and very quiet and is difficult to read and harder to damage, and qi accumulates rather than circulates, so breakthroughs are late and have never failed. Her species' wall is not at nine and is not structural: it is at seventeen, where the flank vessels must be pressurised at once and a longwinter manages one warm gradient for a few weeks in summer and then not again for a year.

appearance.presentation: A longwinter reads as a body that is somewhere else for most of the year: broad and low, heavy with subcutaneous fat, short in the limb, and warm to the touch in a way people reach for and then apologise for. Ilme is the only reader on a shore that has no other readers on it, and the shore has learned to be careful with her for two entirely different reasons, neither of which is her rank.
appearance.age: Seventy-four. Her species ages on a schedule nobody in the setting owns, enormous intake for eleven weeks and then eleven months of almost nothing, and a body that stores a season as fat rather than as qi reaches its own conclusions on that calendar and not on anybody else's.
appearance.build: Broad, low and heavy, with a deep frame, reduced limbs and heavy subcutaneous fat laid over a lowered cold-tolerant core, the particular bulk of a body eleven weeks from finishing a winter rather than eleven weeks from starting one.
appearance.complexion: Pale and slightly waxy, flushed high across the cheekbones in any cold, with the skin of the hands permanently cracked at the knuckles from eleven weeks of working ice for the rest of the year.
appearance.hair: Dark, thick and worn in one coarse braid down the back, re-braided every season and never once for style, because braiding is a thing her people do while standing about waiting for something to happen.
appearance.eyes: Small, dark and slightly hooded, with poor daylight acuity, so she brings her face close to a speaker rather than raising her voice and has apologised for it every single time.
appearance.palette: Rift-shore grey, wet basalt and flat cold light carry her completely. The single accent is a knotted cord at her belt, which is a mark-holder rather than a colour, and the marks in it are not hers: she reads them and lays none, because laying them is somebody else's office on this shore and she has kept that boundary carefully for forty years.
appearance.attire: Fully covered and layered in a fixed order that the household's stores are arranged around: heavy coat, felted mid-layer, a high collar laid over the flank line, thick gloves, and soft boots soled for ice and replaced rather than repaired. She sheds and dons her layers on a calendar, and everybody who stores anything for her knows it.
appearance.marks: The cord burn at the belt where eleven weeks of hauling has held the same weight in the same place, and a notch worn into the left thumb where a sampling vial cap has been opened and closed some thousands of times.
appearance.bearing: Still in the particular way of a person conserving an enormous reserve, moving closer than a stranger finds comfortable, and turning her whole upper body toward a speaker because her hearing is good and her eyesight is not, which reads as warmth and is in fact technique.

canon.role_in_story: The rift at the Realm's edge has stood open long enough to be named, and both sides of it write the same group at the same value, and no qi tide has ever crossed it. A house on that shore marks its own threshold, renews the mark when the frame under it changes, and openly admits that a marked threshold may hold while the frame does not, which is a practice rather than a religion and is built on the absence of a mechanism. The question underneath all of it has a settlement test, and the test is one sentence: a qi value read on the far side, at any time, by anyone not part of the shore's rite. Ilme is the only reader on that shore. Her species is the only population that crosses it, navigates by scent markers laid down deliberately over generations, and can hold two warm gradients at once for a few weeks in summer. She is therefore the one person who could take the reading, and her species is the one population the test excludes, because laying a mark is participation in the rite and participation is the word the test turns on. The answer to the question her whole route depends on can only be brought back by somebody who is not her, and there is nobody on this shore who is not her.
canon.first_appearance: First seen crouched with her cheek near a knotted cord at the edge of a wet basalt shelf, not touching it, counting something on her fingers and then looking up at a shore reader who has come to ask whether the crossing is open, and answering that she does not know and has not known since spring, which is the first time anybody on that shore has heard the word since used about the crossing.
canon.lore:
The mystery is narrow and the evidence is clean: an open tear, a matched value on both sides, and four centuries of ritual with no measured arrival on the far side. A tide is a law value moving through its range on a cycle, so a cycle that never arrives is the entire content of the question. The shore's liturgy was built on the absence of a mechanism and is the only rite in the setting that cannot be falsified, which is also the only reason it survives a falsification attempt. If a qi value is ever read on the far side by somebody outside the rite, the rite becomes a technique and the house loses its only lawful reason to exist.

The shore is one stretch of the Realm's edge, and the rift is there because the top budget is the only one with enough imprints gathered close enough to push one off the end of its range. A rift closes when the value returns in range, so the shore is a door with a timetable, and every power that has ever reached it has built its wall facing the wrong way. That is why this is the only trade route in the setting nobody has been able to close, and why her species is the whole of its traffic: a longwinter reaches far and never stays anywhere, which is exactly what a door with a timetable needs and exactly what a threshold-maker cannot supply, because the house marks the threshold and renews the mark and does not man it.

The body she brings to it is the difficulty. Smell is the navigation system and they track a fixed route over generations, leaving markers on purpose and never returning to them; hearing is good and daylight sight is poor enough that an unfamiliar room is a room she is guessing at. Her soul is held very deep and very quiet, so it is difficult to read and exceptionally hard to damage. Qi accumulates in her rather than circulating, so her breakthroughs are late and rarely fail. She packs a winter as body fat rather than as qi and lowers her core for eleven months, which is superb for carrying and ruinous for inspection: eleven weeks of availability, then a large, warm, immobile target that cannot be woken quickly.

And the mind path is where the ruinous part becomes structural rather than merely inconvenient. What she practises is holding, a sustained construct kept open without being fed, which is the one thing her species can do that no other population has four centuries of practice at. So the question is answered, and answered well, for about eleven weeks a year. Then she goes down. The construct does not survive it. The derivation is gone, and it is re-derived next season, and it is never the same derivation twice, because she has lost the thread that would make it the same, and the route is operated every season on whichever derivation is current.

That is the whole of it and she will not soften it. The species that could settle the question is the species the settlement test excludes, and the exclusion is not a judgement about her honesty. It is structural: the test asks for a reader who is not part of the rite, and her entire navigation is a rite in another substrate, a mark laid on purpose, renewed generation onto generation, and read by whoever comes over the shoulder next. She reads the marks. She does not lay them, and she has kept that boundary carefully for forty years, and the boundary she has kept does not help her at all, because a body that crosses the tear and reads qi there has crossed it on somebody's marker, and that is participation by any honest reading of the word.

And she is not permitted to find out what she would have concluded. She has taken the reading eleven times. She has not carried it back. Nobody on the shore has asked her to, which is either a courtesy or the recognition that a settlement taken by a participant is worth less than no settlement, and she has never established which, and she has noticed that she would rather it stayed unknown.
history: Born on the cold steppe side of the ridge at the far end of a line three generations of her family had walked, timed into the thaw like the rest of them.
Was taken onto the crossing at nine as a child of a mark-holder, which is an ordinary job and the only one on this shore where a nine-year-old's nose is better than an adult's.

Left the laying of marks at nineteen, deliberately, on the ground that reading a marker and writing one are different offices and a reader who also writes cannot be asked what the writing meant, a distinction she has kept for forty years and has never once been thanked for.
Took the reading for the first time at twenty-six, on the far side, stood there long enough to be certain of it, came back, told nobody, and has taken it ten more times since.

Was asked at sixty-one by the house to say what the crossing means, gave the only answer the rite permits, which is a statement about the mark, and has since stopped giving it, because the house began using it to decide the window.

She reads as a comfortable, unhurried, slightly dull woman who is glad to see you, and that reading is entirely accurate and contains none of the content of her life. She is not lonely about the eleven months. She is lonely about the eleven weeks.
